extracted.intended_audience: writers, comedians, and students studying rhetorical devices for humor
extracted.subtask_description: Use rhetorical figures to make lines memorable, rhythmic, and often funny; the page catalogs devices and gives a short rubric for 'rhetorical polish' aimed at producing quotable comedic phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alliteration
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeated initial sounds ("She sells sea shells").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates rhythm and sonic patterning that aids memorability and can add comic emphasis or tongue-in-cheek tone when overused or unexpected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antithesis
rubrics_metrics.description: Contrasting ideas in parallel ("To err is human; to forgive divine").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets up contrast for surprise or ironic reversal; useful in punchlines that hinge on juxtaposition of opposing concepts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anaphora
rubrics_metrics.description: Repeated word at start ("We shall fight on the beaches…").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Builds momentum and expectation; repetition at the beginning can magnify a final unexpected twist or deflate for comic effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Epistrophe
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Echoes and emphasis via repetition at clause ends; can drive a gag by returning to the same terminal word with shifting meaning or context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symploce
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines opening and closing repetition to create a strong rhythmic frame that primes the audience for a punchy final variation or reversal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Polysyndeton
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Slows cadence and piles items for comic accumulation, breathless listing, or mock-solemnity; can be used to exaggerate or lampoon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Asyndeton
rubrics_metrics.description: No conjunctions ("I came, I saw, I conquered").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates staccato, rapid-fire rhythm; useful for punchy, clipped comedic lines or to create deadpan escalation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyperbole
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A core comic device: magnifies traits or situations beyond plausibility for absurdity and emphasis; balance is key to avoid implausible confusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Litotes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Underplays to create ironic contrast; works well for dry, understated humor or to let the audience infer the real scale of praise or insult.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paradox
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates intellectual surprise and a twist in meaning; can produce wry, thought-provoking humor when a paradox reveals an unexpected truth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chiasmus
rubrics_metrics.description: A-B-B-A structure ("Ask not what your country can do for you…").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elegant mirror structure that makes lines feel balanced and quotable; subverting the second half can produce a witty reversal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Antimetabole
rubrics_metrics.description: Words reversed ("Live to eat or eat to live?").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A subtype of chiasmus where identical words are flipped; creates twisty parallelism ideal for punchy aphoristic jokes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Zeugma
rubrics_metrics.description: One word governs two clauses oddly ("She broke his car and his heart").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Produces surprise by shifting the governing word's semantic range; often comic when one governed item is literal and the other figurative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hendiadys
rubrics_metrics.description: One idea expressed by two words ("nice and warm").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can soften or embellish expression; used in humor to inflate mundanity or to create mock-grandiose phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diacope
rubrics_metrics.description: Phrase repeated with words in between ("Bond. James Bond.").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Repetition separated by an intervening element heightens recognition and can produce comedic echoing or a punchline repeat.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tricolon
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tripartite lists are rhetorically satisfying and memorable; in comedy, a three-part rule often sets up an escalating third element as the gag.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enallage
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Breaking grammar intentionally can convey voice, create character-based humor, or yield surprise; must be used deliberately to avoid seeming like a mistake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anadiplosis
rubrics_metrics.description: End of one clause = start of next ("Fear leads to anger; anger leads to hate…").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chains ideas and builds momentum; can be used to escalate absurdity or to link terms toward an ironic payoff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synaesthesia
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combining sensory domains creates striking imagery and unexpected connections useful for surreal or vivid comic descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Epizeuxis
rubrics_metrics.description: Immediate repetition ("alone, alone, all all alone").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct repetition intensifies emotion or absurdity; repetition for comic emphasis can be effective when timed against a deadpan delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pleonasm
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deliberate repetition of meaning can be used for emphasis or to mock verbosity; redundant phrasing can itself be a source of humor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aposiopesis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Elliptical break or sudden cutoff invites the audience to fill in the gap, often leading to comic implication or innuendo.

rubrics_metrics.name: Catachresis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inventive or strained metaphor can produce comic shock or highlight character voice; risky but effective for absurd imagery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhetorical Polish — rhythmic rhetorical figure
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the joke use a rhythmic rhetorical figure?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the line employs devices (alliteration, anaphora, trisyllabic rhythms, etc.) that create flow and musicality which enhance memorability and comedic timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhetorical Polish — parallel structure
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check for balanced, parallel constructions that make a line feel measured and quotable; parallelism often sets up a satisfying payoff or reversal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhetorical Polish — sound patterns
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate use of sonic techniques—assonance, consonance, alliteration—that give lines a catchy audio profile aiding recall and punch delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhetorical Polish — exaggeration/understatement
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decide whether hyperbole or litotes is used purposefully to create contrast, irony, or escalate absurdity rather than as a lazy over- or under-claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rhetorical Polish — quotability ('snap')
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether phrasing is concise, surprising, and memorable enough to be repeated; quotability often derives from rhythm, surprise, and density of meaning.
